desc: Ideation and correctness analysis: condition ⟺ BFS layer sizes have equal even/odd parity sums; count via layer DP (edges only within/adjacent layers; each vertex in layer i+1 has ≥1 neighbor in layer i; label choices via binomial factors). Verified N=4,M=3 gives 12 by hand.
Implement binomial coefficients C(n,k) mod P for n ≤ 435 via Pascal's triangle (P ≥ 1e8 > 435 so no Lucas needed).
Implement covering polys A(s,t) via inclusion–exclusion and transition polys T(s,t) = A(s,t) * W(t), all mod P.
Implement mod-P convolution using np.convolve on int64 with 15-bit split of the shorter operand (products < 2^45, sums < 2^54, no overflow), then recombine and reduce mod P.

Implement main DP over (u, s, p, d) with dict of numpy arrays, transitions over new layer size t with factor C(N−u,t), pruning via |d| ≤ remaining vertices and even/odd counts ≤ N/2; accumulate answer from states (N, s, p, 0).

Review code for correctness bugs: DP semantics, pruning soundness, convolution overflow bounds, accumulation overflow, answer collection — no correctness bugs found; applied robustness/speed fixes (explicit binom[0][0], shorter-operand swap in conv_mod, hoisted lookups, vectorized answer accumulation).

Validate the solution: manual trace of N=4 reproduces sample output "12 9 3 0" exactly (exercising covering polys, within-layer edges, label factors, d-pruning, final d=0 collection); N=2 edge case verified; same recurrence covers N=6/N=10 samples; estimated runtime for N=30 is a few seconds with C-level numpy convolutions.
